record.paper_title: Open problems of the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For the ordered complete graph K_m with vertex set {1,2,...,m}, call two independent edges ij and st nested when i < s < t < j or s < i < j < t. Determine, as a function of n, the smallest integer m such that every 2-coloring of the edges of K_m contains a monochromatic matching of size n whose edges are pairwise non-nested.

evidence.quote:
Two independent edges ij and st are nested, if i < s < t < j or s < i < j < t. If we 2-color the edges, then we would like to find a large monochromatic non-nested matching.
Problem 1.1 Determine the smallest m such that in every 2-coloring of the edges of the
ordered complete graph Km, there is a monochromatic non-nested matching of size n.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the ordered complete graph $K_m$ on the vertex set $\{1, 2, \dots, m\}$ with the natural linear order. Two independent edges $\{i,j\}$ and $\{s,t\}$ (with $i<j$ and $s<t$) are called nested if either $i < s < t < j$ or $s < i < j < t$. A matching is called non-nested if no two of its edges are nested. For a positive integer $n$, determine, as an explicit function of $n$, the smallest integer $m = m(n)$ such that for every 2-coloring of the edges of $K_m$, there exists a monochromatic non-nested matching of size $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on ordered Ramsey-type problems for non-nested matchings provides only partial results and bounds (e.g., extremal counts of the form between $(k-1)n$ and $(k-1)n + \binom{k-1}{2}$), and authors raise this as a conjecture/open question. The exact value of the smallest $m$ guaranteeing a monochromatic non-nested matching of size $n$ in every 2-coloring of $K_m$ does not appear to be determined.

status_evidence.title: Matchings avoiding ordered patterns
status_evidence.snippet: our results and conjectures yield consequences to certain Ramsey-type problems for non-nested matchings and alternating paths
status_evidence.claim: The problem is connected to open Ramsey-type conjectures, with only bounds known.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic spanning trees and matchings in ordered complete graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Every t-colored ordered complete graph contains certain monochromatic non-nested matchings; exact thresholds remain studied.
status_evidence.claim: Related ordered Ramsey matching thresholds are studied with partial results.
